stopBoundaryCorrection.originalRule: The original card required FPS_SMOKE_RENDERER=native and stated that a non-GPU result must be kept without switching renderer or retrying; on timeout, inspect owned processes and artifacts first and do not blindly retry.
stopBoundaryCorrection.violation: Attempt 0 launched software WebGL and exited 1. The next invocation switched to full Chromium with FPS_SMOKE_RENDERER=native and obtained a GPU pass. That is a renderer switch and retry after a non-GPU failure.
stopBoundaryCorrection.withdrawnWording: The previous exit-evidence note called the accepted run the 'prescribed native configuration' and said 'No renderer fallback, no no-sandbox/unsafe flag and no renderer switch was used to obtain the accepted result.' The absence of no-sandbox/unsafe flags is still true for the accepted routes, but the no-renderer-switch claim is false and is withdrawn.
stopBoundaryCorrection.preSpecifiedExecutableIsNotAnExcuse: Pointing FPS_SMOKE_CHROMIUM at an existing executable before the second invocation is allowed by the card, but it does not override the stop condition that had already been triggered by the software result.
stopBoundaryCorrection.forwardRule: On a non-GPU renderer or a timeout, keep the result, stop the corresponding action, and report the gap. Do not switch renderer, do not retry the same capture, and do not present the later success as erasing the earlier deviation.
stopBoundaryCorrection.acceptedEvidenceStatus: The second attempt's functional facts are valid evidence for the side entry, but they do not make the overall card execution compliant and do not establish three-piece art quality.

openIssues.summary: Attempt 0 produced software WebGL and failed; the operator switched to full Chromium and retried to obtain GPU success, violating the card's keep-result/no-switch/no-retry boundary.
openIssues.status: open, not curable after the fact

openIssues.summary: The attempt-0 complete manifest content is retained: it was recovered from the local first-attempt smoke log and is published redacted in this file and exit-evidence.json, with its 21 build hashes matching the second attempt. Not retained: the output-directory report.json contents, browser logs and the raw report.webgl version/renderer/vendor/unmaskedVendor; only the unmaskedRenderer string survives from the historical record.
The failing route's preview port-close proof and complete parent-chain exit record are missing; browser pids 96172 and 50524 exiting 0 do not prove preview or parent-chain teardown.

Retained polling logs partially evidence the 20:43:30.074-20:44:59.647Z gap: samples from 20:43:30.363Z to 20:44:29.306Z contain only receiver worker pid 78372, with own browser/smoke/vite processes absent after 20:43:29.26-20:43:29.50Z. No port probe exists and the final ~30.34s is unsampled, so full cleanup/serial verification before the second start is unproven.
Wall face/corner at player eye height, crouched cover sightline, selected-lamp readability, and the normal combat view with enemy and ally were not captured or judged.

The only art comparison frames are initial deployment #stage captures with the deployment menu and HUD overlaying much of the scene; they cannot verify the three standards' visual quality, and the 0.84% pixel difference is not a quality verdict.
No non-author visual preference judgement and no meaningful second art revision were performed.
GPU frame timing and performance were not measured.
Six-round full match, halftime side switch, end-of-match result and play-again, and human visual/feel/audio acceptance remain unverified.
The run used Node v22.23.2 / npm 10.9.8 while package engines requires >=24; Node 24+ was not validated.
No shared GPU lock existed or was used; cross-task global GPU exclusivity is not proven.
